newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Millennium aims to build on first half rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Millennium aims to build on first half rise.

text.p: British-based Millennium & Copthorne Hotels Plc, riding buoyant markets, said prospects remained bright after unveiling a rise of more than 50 percent in first half profits on Wednesday.
Pre-tax profit for the six months to June 30 climbed to 19.9 million pounds ($31.4 million) from 13.0 million at this stage a year ago. Turnover rose by more than a third to 95.3 million pounds.
"The outlook for the group remains good - the second half has started well with July showing good growth on the same period last year," said chairman Kwek Leng Beng.
"The results of our group tend to be weighted towards the second half of the year and I am confident we will achieve our goals for the year," added Singaporean entrepreneur Kwek in a statement.
Millennium shares had risen 8p to 376.5p by 1100 GMT as the results met expectations, building on Tuesday's 18p gains.
Analysts upgraded their forecasts for the full-year. Brokerage Dresdner Kleinwort Benson raised its pre-tax profit estimate by one million pounds to 49 million.

The company was floated by CDL Hotels International, the hotel arm of Singapore's City Developments Ltd, in April 1996 at a price of 278p. It has a portfolio of 24 mainly four-star hotels in Britain, New York, France and Germany.

Finance Director David Cook said Millennium was seeking acquisitions across the United States and western Europe. But he poured cold water on speculation the company was lining up a 250 million pound bid for Radisson SAS Hotels Worldwide, owned by Scandinavian Airline Systems.

The group's average room rate rose five percent to 80.70 pounds in the first half of the year and Cook said the company may better that in the second half as businessmen resume their travels after the summer lull.
"The months of September, October and November are the strongest for us as the business and conference market picks up," he told reporters.
Cook said there was no sign that the strength of the pound was affecting the company's UK business or reducing spending by foreign hotel guests.
The company reaped the benefits of strong markets in the cities of London, New York and the UK provinces.

But its German and French operations slipped to a 100,000 pound loss. However, this included a one million pound provision to cover the temporary closure of the group's central Paris hotel. The property is being refurbished and will re-open next spring as France prepares to host soccer's World Cup.
